newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks shrug off losses to end modestly higher.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks shrug off losses to end modestly higher.

text.p: After spending much of the day in negative territory, Hong Kong stocks closed modestly higher on Friday as leading blue chips reversed early losses.
The Hang Seng Index gained 20.47 points, or 0.15 percent, to close at 14,062.37 after falling to a session low of 13,932.50.
"Some of the leader stocks are still doing quite well," said Frederick Tsang, head of research BNP PrimeEast Securities.
He pointed to Cheung Kong (Holdings) which hit a record high of HK$78.50 before closing at HK$77.25, up HK$0.75.
"The reversal in HSBC also helped," added Tsang.
HSBC Holdings gained HK$2.00 to HK$220.00.
But turnover fell to HK$12.73 billion on Friday compared with Thursday's HK$16.83 billion as concern about a shakeout in Chinese markets dampened sentiment in the red chip area.
Shanghai's B share index fell 4.88 percent to 84.438 and Shenzhen's B share index slid 7.80 percent to 159.07 points.

"B shares are down quite a bit so that is spilling over into the red chips in Hong Kong," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at NAVA SC Securities. "We have had a big move up and we are getting ready for profit-taking," he added.
The Hang Seng Index advanced 131.57 points, or 0.94 percent, this week.
Tsang said the market needed high levels of turnover to keep the momentum going but had lacked that support on Friday.
Turnover this session was the lowest in more than two weeks.
"The stock market needs trading volume to support prices at higher levels. The higher the level, the more trading volume is needed to support the market," said Tsang.
He said share prices may move sideways next week ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve meeting on Tuesday.
"That is probably why we had the Friday afternoon blah," said Galbraith, adding that investors were taking a wait-and-see approach.
In the property sector, Henderson Land rose HK$0.25 to HK$72.00 and Hysan Development gained HK$0.15 to HK$23.60.
But in the finance sector, only HSBC managed to make gains on Friday. Hang Seng Bank shed HK$1.25 to HK$92.50 and Bank of East Asia fell HK$0.05 to HK$28.15.
CITIC Pacific fell HK$0.10 to HK$42.80 and COSCO Pacific shed HK$0.30 to HK$10.10. The H-share index slipped 4.34 points, or 0.43 percent, to 1,012.38.
May Hang Seng Index futures rose 80 points to 14,040.
